BUYING GUIDE / YOUR NEXT QUOTE

Two quotes. One clear comparison.

Match the vehicle and separate the numbers before deciding which offer fits.

By Rishi · AutoTech Review · October 2, 2026

A lower monthly payment can come from a longer loan, a larger down payment or a different vehicle. Put two written offers side by side before choosing. Use the same currency and market, and leave personal information out of any notes or links you share.

Start with the exact car

Record the model year, trim, drivetrain, factory options and whether the vehicle is new, used or a demonstrator. Ask for the VIN or stock number. For a used vehicle, compare mileage, condition, service history and the warranty actually included.

Ask for the vehicle price and an itemized total

Request the selling price before financing, then a list of freight or destination charges, dealer fees, taxes, registration and add-ons. Ask which items are optional, whether they can be removed and how the total changes. Do not assume the same fee rules apply in every province or state.

Fields to request in both written offers
FieldWhat to match or clarify
VehicleYear, trim, drivetrain, options, stock number and condition
Price and feesSelling price, mandatory charges, optional products and tax
FinancingAPR, term, amount financed, payment frequency and total repayment
Upfront moneyDown payment, deposit terms and trade-in shown separately
TimingOffer expiry, delivery date and any availability conditions

Compare finance terms separately

Ask for the annual percentage rate, length of the loan, number and frequency of payments, amount financed and total amount payable. Request the terms without a trade-in first, then add the trade-in so you can see its effect. A longer repayment period can reduce each payment while changing the total you repay.

For a lease, also compare the distance allowance, upfront amount, term, end-of-lease purchase option and the stated wear or excess-distance charges. Confirm whether advertised payments include tax. Get any deposit refund conditions in writing before paying.

Add the costs of your own driving

Get insurance quotes for the exact vehicles and ask about the service schedule. Compare fuel using your actual annual distance and local fuel price in the annual fuel-cost calculator. It is a fuel estimate; it does not calculate financing, taxes, insurance or total ownership cost.

Leave with a decision you can explain

Write one sentence for each shortlisted car: “I prefer this because…” If the answer is only a payment, return to the itemized total. If the answer is a feature, confirm it is included on the car in the offer. Use the test-drive checklist for the questions a quote cannot answer.

Official consumer resources

  • Financial Consumer Agency of Canada: compare auto-financing
  • U.S. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau: compare auto-loan offers
